hens_rule_text: Fewer than 6 fowl kept as household pets are allowed without a permit in most residential zones. Keeping 6 or more fowl, or any fowl outside that pet exemption, needs a city permit.
permit_notes: No permit is needed to keep fewer than 6 rabbits or fowl as household pets. A permit from El Paso Animal Services (about $35/year) is required for 6 or more, or outside a farm-ranch or stockyard-zoned district. No more than 3 roosters are allowed where fowl are kept at all.
setback_notes: Enclosures must be at least 30 ft from any private residence, hotel, apartment, hospital, church or school, or as close as 20 ft if separated by a public alley and a solid fence or wall at least 6 ft high.
coop_rules: Fowl must be kept in a secure pen or enclosure; manure must be removed from yards, cages and enclosures at least twice weekly and disposed of so the premises stay free of nuisance.
zoning_notes: Permit is not required in a farm-ranch district or a zoning district where a stockyard or stable is permitted. Elsewhere the fewer-than-6 pet exemption applies.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Title 7, Ch. 7.24 (Livestock and Other Animals), Sec. 7.24.050
